neighbours.label: contact or junction between rock bodies in a geological description (contact, junction, intrusive, penetration)
fire: Near the quarry, the basalt has a sharp contact with the underlying limestone.
Geologists mapped the junction between the granite and the slate.
The intrusive body cuts across older sedimentary layers.
Baked shale is exposed along the contact with the dike.
An unconformity marks the junction of the two formations.
Veins of quartz follow the contact between the schist and gneiss.
Water penetration along joints has weakened the sandstone.
The lava flow rests in contact with a red soil horizon.
quiet: Close to the mine, the basalt is dark and fine-grained.
Geologists measured the age of the granite with zircons.
Older sedimentary layers contain many marine fossils.
The shale here is rich in organic carbon.
Both formations were deposited in a shallow sea.
Quartz crystals in the schist sparkle in sunlight.
Wind erosion has rounded the sandstone cliffs.
The lava flow cooled into hexagonal columns.
